sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB /
NH-844/ CR / 45 / 2021-22 dated 26.02.2024 pertaining to Survey No.162 measuring 222.95 Square Meters of Madivala village, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru Urban District.
A.P. No.33/2024 .2.

The definite case of the petitioner is that the property of respondent No.1 bearing Survey No.162 measuring 222.95 Square Meters of Madivala village, Anekal Taluk has been acquired under Preliminary Notification dated 24.01.2019 and Final Notification dated 23.01.2020.

The respondent No.3 passed the award and awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.63,73,902/- after deducting the TDS of Rs.7,08,211/- in respect of 222.95 Square Meters, which has been received by the respondent No.1 under protest.

Subsequently, on 22.10.2021 the respondent No.1 has filed the application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.5,000/-
per Square feet.
Accordingly, the application is taken by the respondent No.2 for consideration.

.3. Thereafter, the Arbitrator held an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ / ARB / NH-844 /
CR / 47/46/45/44/2021-22 dated 26.02.2024.
.4.
Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section A.P. No.33/2024 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting aside the following:
:GROUNDS:
The petitioner claims that the impugned is perverse, patently illegal, capricious and goes against the very fundamentals of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

Further the lands of the respondent No.1 are acquired in part and hence there is a necessity to enhance the compensation in a scientific manner by placing reliance upon the guidance value notification.

The observation of the respondent No.2 is contrary to Section 3-G(7)(a) of the NH Act since the market value has to be determined as on 23.01.2019 which is the date of Preliminary Notification and not thereafter.

Further the respondent No.2 has held that the market value already redetermined by in the National Highways Authority Of India vs Anil Kumar E on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5924453/
2 case of LAQ / ARB / NH-844 / CR /186/2022- 23 filed by one Nataraj pertaining to Madivala village is applicable to the instant case, wherein the respondent No.2 has held that the respondent No.1 is entitled to Rs. 4,422/- per Square Meters towards enhanced compensation in case of NA lands and in case of a agricultural lands, the claimants were entitled to 50% addition on the A.P. No.33/2024 guidance value prescribed in the notification.

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 has taken the contents of the operative portion of the impugned Arbitral Award from some other case without any application of mind.

Further the copy of the sale deed dated 22.11.2019 was never produced by the respondent No.1 in the arbitral proceedings and there was no opportunity given to the petitioner at any point of time to rebut the same.
The reliance upon the sale deed is in utter contravention of Section 3-G(7)(a) of NH Act.

Further the sale deed was executed in respect of Survey No. 184 that was nowhere near the subject lands and there was no document produced by the respondent No.1 to indicate that the development on the subject lands as on the date of Preliminary Notification was same as that of the lands forming a subject matter of the sale deed dated 22.11.2019.
Further there is no document produced to indicate whether the amenities if any were in existence and developed as on 24.01.2019 itself.
Further there is no reasons assigned for awarding 50% of Rs. 8,845/- per Square Meters as enhancement, which is not in accordance with the provisions of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

Further the respondent No.2 has not assigned any reasons for re-determining A.P. No.33/2024 the compensation amount at Rs.14,422/- per Square Meters especially when the parties had neither agreed that no reasons were to be given nor the impugned Arbitral Award is an award on agreed terms under Section 30 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
Further the respondent No.2 had adopted a random formula of enhancement of 50% irrespective of the nature of case or the claims of the lands owners.
There was absolutely no legal or rational basis behind the impugned Arbitral Award except for suiting the needs of the land owners.
The impugned Arbitral Award was passed on 26.02.2024, the certified copy of the Arbitral Award was received by the petitioner on 12.03.2024.

The stipulated period of 3 months commences from 12.03.2024 the petition is filed within 3 months from the date of receipt of the impugned Arbitral Award by the petitioner and hence, the petition is in time.
Among other grounds, prayed for relief claimed in the petition.

.5. The respondent No. 1 to 3 though served with the notice, the respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel, the respondents 2 and 3 not chosen to appear before this Court to resist the petition and hence, the A.P. No.33/2024 entire records in LAQ / ARB / NH-844 / CR / 45 / 2021-22 dated 26.02.2024 secured from the Arbitrator.

.6. On the basis of above, the point for consideration is that:
"Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?"
.7.
Heard the arguments.

REASONS .8.
Point:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note the admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The respondent No.1 Sri. Anil Kumar E is an owner of the property bearing Survey No.162 measuring to an extent of 222.95 Square Meters of Madivala village and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-844 under Preliminary Notification dated 24.01.2019 and Final Notification dated 23.01.2020,
is an admitted fact.
It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.63,73,902/- after deducting the TDS was disbursed to the respondent No. 1 as compensation.

.9. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the respondent No. 1 Sri. Anil A.P. No.33/2024 Kumar E filed an application on 22.10.2021 before the respondent No.2 claiming that he is entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs.5,000/- per Square feet.
On the basis of said application, the respondent No. 2 held an inquiry and passed order in LAQ / ARB / NH- 844 / CR / 45 / 2021-22 dated 26.02.2024.
The respondent No.2 in its order redetermined the market value at Rs.14,422/- from Rs. 10,000/- Square Meters (Rs.14,422/- - Rs.10,000/- = 4,422/- Square Meters).

The respondent No. 2 in its order enhanced the compensation at Rs.4,422/- per Square meter by adding Rs.10,000/- per Square Meters to the compensation decided by the respondent No. 3.
.10.

In the case on hand, the LAO/ respondent No.3 passed the award under New Act i.e., Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 being not satisfied with the said award passed by the LAO / respondent No.3, filed an application before the respondent No.2 / Arbitrator and A.P. No.33/2024 Special Deputy Commissioner seeking enhancement of compensation.

Accordingly, the respondent No.2 /
Arbitrator vide order dated 26.02.2024 enhanced the compensation.

The said enhancement is under challenge in this petition with the claim of the petitioner that the LAO has passed the award by following due procedures as contemplated under Sections 26 to 30 along with first schedule of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and claims that there is no scope for the Arbitrator to enhance the compensation and the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 ought to have confirmed the award passed by the respondent No.3/
National Highways Authority Of India vs Anil Kumar E on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5924453/
4 LAO.
.11. In view of the aforesaid definite contention, it is just and necessary to see what are the criteria to determine the market value of the acquired land as per new Act has to be considered by this Court.
Section 26 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, A.P. No.33/2024 2013 speaks about determination of market value of the land by the Collector, Section 27 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about determination of amount of compensation,
Section 28 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about parameter considered by the Collector in determination of the award and Section 29 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about determination of value of the things attached to the land or building.

sentences.text: Section 30 of Land Acquisition Act speaks about award of solatium.

In the context of this case, it is just and relevant to note Sections 26 and 28 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013,
that reads as under:
"26. Determination of market value of land by Collector- (1) The Collector shall adopt the following criteria in assessing A.P. No.33/2024 and determining the market value of the land, namely:--
(a) the minimum land value, if any, specified in the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 for the registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell, as the case may be, in the area, where the land is situated; or (b) the average sale price for similar type of land situated in the nearest village or nearest vicinity area; or (c) consented amount of compensation as agreed upon under sub-section (2) of section 2 in case of acquisition of lands for private companies or for public private partnership projects, whichever is higher:

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Provided that the date for determination of market value shall be the date on which the notification has been issued under section 11".

entities.text: National Highways Authority Of India vs Anil Kumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The first schedule to the Act is in accordance with Section 30(2) of the New Act which shows that the Collector shall issue individual awards detailing the particulars of compensation payable and the details of payment of the compensation as specified in the first A.P.
No.33/2024 schedule.

In the aforesaid facts whenever there is an application for enhancement of compensation before the Arbitrator is filed then it is the duty of the Arbitrator to see that whether the LAO followed Sections 26 to 30 of the New Act along with first schedule to the Act.
If at all the award has been passed in-consonance with the aforesaid provisions of law/new Act, certainly the Arbitrator cannot intervene with the award passed by the LAO.

Therefore, in the case on hand, it is for the petitioner to prove that the award passed by the LAO / respondent No.3 is in-consonance with the aforesaid provisions of law and the respondent No.1 has to prove that the award passed by the LAO / respondent No.3 is not in consonance with the aforesaid provision of law.
As such, he has filed the petition before the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 and the respondent No.2 by considering all those facts enhanced the compensation.

.12. The definite grievance of the petitioner in this case is that the Arbitrator has enhanced the compensation on the basis of the sale deed that was not A.P. No.33/2024 at all in existence at the time of Preliminary Notification and also claims that the said sale deed was not at all placed before the respondent No.2 and the said sale deed was either pleaded or claimed by the respondent No.1 in the application filed for enhancement of compensation and the respondent No.1 is also not filed the said document.

The petitioner further claims that the petitioner is totally unaware of the said sale deed and the Arbitrator enhanced the compensation on the basis of the said sale deed that has been admittedly executed 10 months after the preliminary notification and the petitioner claims that the award is liable to be set aside.
.13. I have closely perused the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2.

The Arbitrator till the 2nd paragraph at page No. 6 of her judgment not stated any reason for her award but only stated National Highways Authority Of India vs Anil Kumar E on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5924453/
6 about the respective contentions of the parties as well as acquisition of property by issuing notifications.

entities.text: National Highways Authority Of India vs Anil Kumar E
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the last paragraph of the judgment/award, it is observed by A.P. No.33/2024 the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 that claimant/ respondent No.1 has produced certified copy of the sale deed dated 22.11.2019 and as per the said sale deed, the property measuring 139.29 Square Meters in khatha No. 5856/99 in Survey No. 184 had been sold for total consideration of Rs.26,25,000/-
i.e., Rs. 18,845/- per Square Meter.
On the basis of the said sale deed the LAO has awarded the additional compensation.
Surprisingly this Court is unable to find the said sale deed in the trial Court records.
The Arbitrator in the award at page No.3, 2nd paragraph on- wards stated about the claim of petitioner wherein there was a reference of sale deed relied by the claimant.
The petitioner filed the claim statement before the arbitrator is dated 11.01.2022.
The said statement nowhere discloses about the sale deed relied by the Arbitrator in the judgment to determine the market value.
Therefore it is clear that the respondent No.1 not claimed the enhancement of the compensation on the basis of the sale deed referred by the Arbitrator in the judgment.

It is relevant to note that even according to the Arbitrator, the sale deed relied by the Arbitrator in the judgment is relating to the property in Survey No.184 and the property involved in this case is Sy. No.162.
Whether both properties are adjacent to each other and whether market value of the properties are identical or not is not made known to the Court.
.15 . Further undisputedly the said sale deed is dated 22.11.2019 i.e., subsequent to the Preliminary Notification.

As per the proviso to Section 26, date for determination of market value shall be the date on which the notification has been issued under Section 11. Section 11 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about Preliminary Notification.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
As such, the Arbitrator ought not to have considered the said sale deed.
.16.

Further the Arbitrator in the order assigned the reason for enhancement of compensation that the enhancement is in accordance with enhancement made A.P. No.33/2024 in a case of Nataraj in LAQ / ARB / NH-844 / CR / 186 /2022-23.

Even the said award is not found in the trial Court records and there is no material on record to show that the respondent No.1 insisted the Arbitrator to award the amount of compensation equivalent to the award of compensation awarded in the said case of Nataraj.
.17.
The petitioner also claimed that whatever the document relied by the respondent No. 2 for enhancing the compensation is not brought to the notice of the petitioner before passing the award/judgment.
The award also discloses that the photographs produced by the petitioner to show development of properties but such photographs are not found in the trial Court records.
Accordingly, claimed that such award is liable to be set aside as per Section 24 of National Highways Authority Act.
In this context, the petitioner relied on the decision reported in (2019) 15 SCC 131 in a case of Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs. National Highways Authority of India.

entities.text: Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs. National Highways Authority of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is A.P. No.33/2024 true that in the said decision, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that whatever the document relied by the Arbitrator shall be brought to the notice of the parties, so that the parties can make submission or give a rebuttal evidence about such documents.

7

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, in the case on hand, such sale deed dated 22.11.2019 and the award passed in the case of Nataraj as well as photographs are not found in the record received from the Arbitrator.

.18. The claim of the petitioner is that the respondent No.3 passed the award in accordance with Sections 26 to 30 as well as first schedule of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In this context, the petitioner produced guidance value of the acquired land which is published in Gazette notification dated 01.01.2019.

As per the said document, the market value determined for the properties at Madivala village is at Rs.10,000/- per Square Meter along with determination of market value A.P.
No.33/2024 for all types of land and building etc. Section 26(1)(a)

states that the market value, if any, specified in the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 (2 of 1899) for the registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell, as the case may be, in the area, where the land is situated is to be considered to determine the market value of the acquired property.
Therefore, as per the said provision, the Arbitrator has to determine the market value of the acquired land on the basis of the market value specified in the Indian Stamp Act.

In this case, as per the aforesaid Gazette notification, the market value is fixed at Rs.10,000/- per Square Meter and accordingly the LAO determined the market value and added other statutory benefits.
Undisputedly the said amount has been accepted by the LAO and the compensation was decided on the basis of the said guidance value published in Gazette notification.

When the LAO considered the said market value certainly the Arbitrator ought to have considered the said fact and the Arbitrator in the judgment have not given any A.P. No.33/2024 special reason that why guidance value published in the Gazette notification on 01.01.2019 is not applicable to the facts of this case and how the market value determined in the subsequent sale deed can be accepted as the market value to the acquired property is not at all explained in the judgment.

.19. It is also not the case of the petitioner before the LAO or Arbitrator that the respondent No.3 /
LAO has not awarded the compensation as stated in the aforesaid provision of law.

The award /
judgment passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 also nowhere discloses that the LAO has not considered the parameter of the aforesaid provision of law i.e., Sections 26 to 30 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 to determine the market value.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Gazette notification produced by the petitioner sufficiently discloses that the respondent No.3/ LAO considered the guidance value for registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell and awarded the said A.P. No.33/2024 amount as compensation.

When the LAO has granted the compensation as per Section 26(1)(a) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, certainly the Arbitrator is estopped from enhancing the compensation.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Arbitrator in the aforesaid judgment nowhere stated or discussed or pointed out that the Arbitrator has not followed the aforesaid provisions of law in determining the market value.
It is also not the case of the respondent No.1 before the respondent No.2 that the LAO has not passed the individual award.
Therefore, it is clear that the respondent No.3 / LAO has passed individual award by considering all the relevant facts.
Under such circumstances, certainly the award passed by the LAO cannot be set aside or modified or changed.
In view of all these facts, certainly the award passed by the Arbitrator cannot be accepted and that should be intervened by the Court.

Hence, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to intervene with the A.P. No.33/2024 award passed by the Arbitrator and the award is liable to be set aside.

Accordingly, the above point is held in the National Highways Authority Of India vs Anil Kumar E on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5924453/
8 affirmative.
